claims.text: The initial alloy is a non-equilibrium, supersaturated solid solution produced by rapid solidification or an analogous nonequilibrium process.
Complex concentrated or high-entropy alloys can develop microstructures containing both solid solutions and intermetallic phases.
Thermal or environmental exposure causes localized Mg segregation in the metastable solid-solution matrix.
Localized Mg segregation promotes nucleation and growth of Mg-rich intermetallic compounds.
The proposed Mg-rich intermetallic compounds preferentially form at grain boundaries and interfaces.
Intermetallic precipitation locally depletes the surrounding matrix of Mg.
The precipitates form brittle intermetallic networks.
Mg-rich intermetallic precipitation disrupts the continuity or adherence of protective oxide and passivation layers.
Disruption of protective surface layers by intermetallic precipitation accelerates corrosion relative to the metastable single-phase condition.
Disruption of protective surface layers by intermetallic precipitation accelerates high-temperature oxidation relative to the metastable single-phase condition.
The relevant onset and progression of intermetallic formation typically occur between approximately 300 and 500 °C over tens to hundreds of hours.
A critical temperature-time boundary separates retention of the supersaturated solid solution from intermetallic precipitation.
Above the critical temperature-time boundary, in situ characterization will reveal nucleation of Mg-rich intermetallics.
Below the proposed nucleation boundary, the single-phase supersaturated microstructure will be retained.
Retention of the single-phase microstructure will preserve near-initial corrosion and oxidation resistance.
The as-processed baseline has minimal or no second-phase precipitates and a uniform single-phase solid solution.
The as-processed baseline exhibits stable passivation behavior.
The exact precipitation-onset kinetics and effects of environmental variables such as pH and atmospheric composition are insufficiently characterized.
